title: Stop use of neck force, RCMP told
article: RCMP officers should stop grabbing suspects by the neck to prevent them from swallowing evidence, a B.C. coroner's jury has said.

The inquest into the July 31, 2008 death of 22-year-old Surrey resident Brandon Whitelaw ruled the death an accident Wednesday, but found it was the result of "choking from object (sic) in airway during restraint" by Surrey Mounties.

The jury said Mounties should cease the practice of using "force as applied to the neck area of individuals attempting to swallow evidence (i.e. drugs)" until it has been reviewed by "field experts" as well as medical and legal experts "to decide on the best practice to deal with such situations."
Whitelaw died after he was arrested by police in Whalley near a suspected crack shack in the Ravine Road area.
A vehicle that left the scene was followed by police and subsequently stopped near 106 Avenue and 132 Street.
Whitelaw, a passenger in the car, died after he swallowed a plastic bag containing 11 rocks of crack cocaine.
The inquest jury said "acute methamphetamine toxicity" was a contributing factor in the death.
The three-day hearing wrapped up Wednesday in Burnaby.
RCMP spokesman Insp. Tim Shields said the inquest findings will be reviewed by the force.
"We will study the jury recommendations before making a decision," Shields said Thursday.

The inquest also suggested paramedics should be equipped with gear that can extract objects from the throat of a person with a plugged airway, and called for additional first aid training for officers in "specialized high risk units where the nature of their duties would require them to perform life saving procedures."
Whitelaw was the third man to die in Surrey RCMP custody during a six week period in 2008.
On July 1 of that year, Ryan Wagemans, 24, of Langley died in hospital after he was involved in a scuffle with security on a Coast Mountain bus and was subsequently restrained by RCMP officers.
His death was ruled accidental by a coroner's inquest, the result of "acute methamphetamine intoxication" and struggling with arresting officers.
On June 19, David Stitt, 46, died in hospital after an altercation with police at a residence on Crescent Road.
The inquest into the Stitt death is set for May 18-20.
